title: Sketch-Based Anomaly Detection in Streaming Graphs

problem.claim: Assign anomaly scores to edges and subgraphs in a dynamic graph stream online using constant time and memory.

gap.claim: Existing work detects anomalous edges or anomalous subgraphs, but not both.

contributions.claim: Extends the count-min sketch data structure to a higher-order sketch that preserves dense subgraph structure as dense submatrices.
Proposes four online algorithms using the enhanced data structure to detect both edge and graph anomalies.
The proposed approach processes each edge and graph in constant memory and constant update time per newly arriving edge.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their four online algorithms outperform state-of-the-art baselines on four real-world datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online anomaly scoring is sought for edges and subgraphs in dynamic graph streams under constant time and memory constraints.
Prior work addresses anomalous edges or anomalous subgraphs separately.
The paper extends count-min sketch to a higher-order sketch that preserves dense subgraph structure.
Four online algorithms detect edge and graph anomalies with constant resource bounds, and the authors report improved performance over baselines on four real-world datasets.
The authors characterize the method as the first streaming approach combining dense subgraph search with constant-memory and constant-time graph anomaly detection.

source_observation.claim: A higher-order sketch preserves dense subgraph structure as dense submatrices.

interpretation.claim: Structure-preserving summaries can support streaming detection of higher-order graph anomalies.

application.claim: Use compact graph summaries that retain task-relevant dense structure when anomaly detection must operate under strict streaming resource limits.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach remains effective for graph patterns that are not dense subgraphs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four algorithms or their individual mechanisms.
The abstract does not identify the four datasets, baseline methods, evaluation metrics, or reported performance values.
The abstract does not provide formal guarantees or implementation details for the constant-time and constant-memory bounds.
